title: Tekmar 274: DHW priority lockout or tank not reaching setpoint
equipment: Tekmar 274 boiler control with domestic hot water

options.label: Space heating is held off by DHW
DHW tank does not reach setpoint

h1.text: Does the display show a DHW ERROR?

r_dhwerr.cause: A DHW sensor and a DHW demand were applied at the same time.
fix: The tank will not be heated until the externally powered DHW demand is removed. A powered demand with the DHW sensor enabled generates the error and both demands are ignored.
Use one demand source only: either the DHW sensor, or a powered demand with the sensor set to Off.

h2.text: Which DHW source is calling: a powered demand (aquastat or relay across terminals 23 and 24), the DHW tank sensor, or a tN4 setpoint control?

r_stuck.cause: A powered demand is registered when 20 to 260 V (ac) is across terminals 23 and 24, so a stuck aquastat or relay will hold a permanent demand.
fix: Have the tech measure across terminals 23 and 24 with the aquastat satisfied. If voltage remains, find the stuck aquastat, relay or wiring.
Also compare how long heating has been held off with the DHW Priority Override time (see the override result).

r_sens.cause: With a DHW sensor, demand starts when the tank drops 1/2 the DHW differential below setpoint and ends 1/2 above it.
fix: Check the sensor temperature against the tank and the DHW setpoint and differential.
Remember a shorted or open DHW sensor stops DHW heating (it does not make a false demand); DHW heating resumes when the sensor is repaired.

r_tn4.cause: A tN4 setpoint control in DHW mode sends the demand over the bus.
fix: Check that device for a call stuck on, and its tank temperature setting.

t1.text: Does the display show a DHW sensor short or open circuit?

r_sensor_err.cause: With the DHW sensor faulted the 274 stops heating the DHW tank.
fix: Test the sensor and wiring per Data Brochure D 070 by measuring the actual tank temperature and the sensor resistance.
DHW tank heating resumes once the sensor problem is corrected.

t2.text: Is a DHW demand showing on the display?

r_nodem.cause: The control does not see a DHW demand.
fix: Demand with a sensor starts only after the tank drops 1/2 the DHW differential below setpoint.
DHW demand is ignored in the Away scene, and a powered demand is ignored during UnOccupied or Sleep when DHW UnOccupied is set to Off.
DHW mode must not be set to OFF, and DHW operation needs the Pump Sequencer DIP switch off.

t3.text: Ask the tech to test the DHW pump relay (terminals 17-18) and confirm the DHW circulator or valve runs when the DHW symbol shows. Does it operate?

r_pump.cause: The DHW pump or valve output is not working.
fix: Follow the Testing the Wiring steps for the DHW and primary pump terminals 17-18, then check the pump or valve and its wiring.

r_cap.cause: The tank is being called and pumped, so capacity or limits may be the issue.
fix: With a DHW sensor demand the boilers aim for 40 F above the tank temperature, never above Boil MAX. A tank setpoint high compared to Boil MAX cannot be reached.

DHW Priority Override (modes 2 and 4, and 5 with a tN4 DHW device) ends priority after 15 minutes at design outdoor temperature to 2 hours at 70 F or above, then space heating resumes, so a long recovery may be cut short.
Check boiler capacity and the DHW exchanger or tank.
